review_candidates.title: Senior Financial Accountant
review_candidates.description: The Opportunity We are looking for a hands-on, technically strong Senior Financial Accountant to own the financial accounting for Lumify’s group of training businesses, as well as intercompany and group consolidation. Reporting to the Financial Controller and working closely with our Philippines-based Finance Manager, you will lead month-end close, the 13-week cashflow forecast for the Australian business, and audit and compliance deliverables. You will be the technical anchor of the team, making sure reporting is accurate, reconciled, on time, and able to withstand audit, board, and lender scrutiny. This role would suit someone who is technically rigorous with a strong reconciliation mindset, works independently to tight close deadlines, escalates issues early, and improves processes proactively rather than working around them. You'll also lead by example on quality and help lift the technical standard of the wider team. This is a permanent full-time position. Lumify is a hybrid workplace, with 4 days in the office, and 1 day working from home. Key Responsibilities: Group Consolidation & Reporting: Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation across all group entities, including reconciling intercompany balances and posting elimination journals. Prepare consolidated inputs for the monthly board pack and lender reporting, including underlying EBITDA normalisations and covenant compliance calculations. Cashflow & Liquidity: Build, maintain and own the 13-week rolling cashflow forecast for the Australian entities, driven by debtor collections, supplier terms, deferred revenue, payroll, GST/BAS and financing timing. Model downside scenarios and flag liquidity risks, cash troughs and covenant headroom issues early to the Financial Controller, with recommended actions. Month-End & Balance Sheet Integrity: Own the month-end close for Lumify’s entities, delivering and reviewing journals on time. Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, applying AASB 15 (deferred revenue, prepaid training credits and breakage) and AASB 16 (leases) correctly. Statutory, Audit & Compliance: Act as the primary point of contact for audit fieldwork and prepare statutory financial statements and notes for group and entity accounts. Prepare and lodge monthly BAS and payroll tax returns for the AU entities. Process, Systems & Controls: Improve and standardise consolidation and cashflow methods, building automation into recurring reconciliations and reporting using Business Central, Excel and Power BI. Maintain and monitor key financial controls, including journal approval, segregation of duties, bank reconciliations and delegations of authority. About You CA or CPA qualified 5+ years of post-qualification experience, including multi-entity group reporting Strong working knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards (AASB/IFRS) Demonstrated experience preparing multi-entity, multi-currency group consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and FX translation A track record of owning audits and consolidations end to end, not just contributing to them Advanced Excel modelling (driver-based, scenario logic) and working Power BI skills (Power Query, data modelling, DAX) Hands-on experience with Business Central and Xero Able to explain technical positions clearly to non-accountants and senior stakeholders Comfortable working with a distributed team across AU, NZ and the Philippines A background in Big 4 or mid-tier audit, followed by commercial group finance, is highly regarded Employee Benefits Centrally located Sydney office, right next to Central Station in Haymarket $2,000 referral bonus for bringing great people into the team Birthday leave and volunteering leave Wellbeing support, including EAP 2 days paid study leave to support your personal development Percipio membership, giving you access to thousands of professional development courses Free access to every training course across Lumify's group of companies About us Lumify Group is the largest provider of professional training in Australia, with offices around the country, as well as in New Zealand and the Philippines. With deep expertise over 30 years across Information Technology and Professional Development training, we work with enterprise, government and corporate clients to lift organisational capability through essential training, upskilling and reskilling, backed by a brand that government and blue-chip clients already trust. We exist to help people and organisations build the capability to meet the skills gaps of the future. We are proud to be a three-time Australian Business Awards Employer of Choice (2023–2025). review_candidates.description: Company Description Mountainview Health & Wellness Ltd. is a community-focused healthcare provider serving individuals and families in the Greater Vancouver Metropolitan Area. The organization emphasizes integrated, patient-centered care that combines clinical excellence with preventive health and wellness services. Interdisciplinary collaboration, respectful communication, and evidence-based practice are central to how care teams support diverse patient populations. Team members are encouraged to contribute ideas, develop professionally, and help shape innovative approaches to primary and specialty care. The workplace culture values inclusivity, continuous improvement, and high-quality patient outcomes. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Nurse Practitioner role based in the Greater Vancouver Metropolitan Area. The Nurse Practitioner will provide comprehensive patient assessments, diagnose and manage acute and chronic conditions, order and interpret diagnostic tests, and prescribe medications and treatments in accordance with applicable regulations. Day-to-day responsibilities include delivering primary care visits, developing care plans, offering health education and counseling, and coordinating care with physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals. The role also involves documenting clinical encounters accurately, participating in quality improvement initiatives, and contributing to the development of clinical protocols and best practices. The Nurse Practitioner will engage in collaborative decision-making with patients and care teams to support person-centered, culturally sensitive care. Qualifications Current Nurse Practitioner licensure (or eligibility for licensure) in the relevant jurisdiction, with good standing and no practice restrictions. Graduate-level education in nursing (e.g., Master’s or Doctoral degree in Nursing, Nurse Practitioner program) with training in primary care or relevant specialty. Demonstrated clinical skills in assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, and management of acute and chronic conditions across diverse populations. Strong ability to collaborate within an interdisciplinary team, including physicians, nurses, allied health professionals, and administrative staff. Proficiency in electronic medical records (EMR), documentation standards, and basic digital literacy for clinical and administrative workflows. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide clear health education and support patient self-management. Commitment to person-centered, culturally responsive, and non-discriminatory care, including working effectively with diverse communities. Experience in community health, family practice, or wellness-focused settings is an asset. Proven organizational and time-management skills, including the ability to prioritize caseloads and manage a full-time clinical schedule. Ongoing commitment to professional development and staying current with evidence-based guidelines and regulatory requirements.
